ios.desc:
The internet. As it should be.

Firefox is a private web browser designed to protect your data, block trackers and make browsing fast, secure and simple. Whether you’re looking for an incognito browser, a private search experience, or a reliable browser for everyday use, Firefox puts you first.

Why people choose Firefox:

More privacy, less tracking – Firefox automatically blocks social media trackers, cross-site cookies, crypto miners and fingerprinting scripts.
Private browsing that protects you – Open private tabs that don’t save your history, searches, or cookies. Lock them with your device security for extra protection.
Fewer ads, less clutter – Turn on built-in ad blocking to cut down on distracting ads, leaving more room for what you actually came to see.
Fast, smooth performance – Load pages faster by blocking trackers and reducing unnecessary data usage.
Get Quick Answers – Ask Firefox a question by voice for a clear answer without digging through search results. 
Quick page summaries – Shake your phone to cut through long pages and get the key points.
Tabs that work for you – Easily organize and switch between tabs and sync them across devices to pick up where you left off.
Focus without distractions – Reader View strips away clutter, while picture-in-picture lets you multitask with videos.
Passwords made simple – Generate, store and autofill passwords securely.
Search your way – Use your preferred private search engine or switch easily from the search bar.
Control your experience – Add extensions like ad blockers, customize settings and choose how you browse.
AI on your terms – Turn AI completely off or customize it feature by feature.
Sync across devices – Access your bookmarks, tabs and passwords anywhere you use Firefox.
Make it yours – Customize your home screen, layout and shortcuts for a more personal browsing experience.

Private by default.

Firefox is built to protect you. Enhanced Tracking Protection automatically blocks common trackers, and you can also turn on the built-in ad blocker for more control over your browsing and fewer distracting ads. When you need more privacy, private browsing mode ensures your history, searches and cookies aren’t saved.

You're definitely gaining even more instability than with Chrome.  And by that, I mean, insane random changes.

Just look at, for example, the recent madness with Firefox on Android.  They effectively pushed a beta about 6 weeks ago, removed tonnes of features, made many menu items difficult to navigate to, removed compatibility with almost all add-ons, it's slower, it crashes for many constantly, it's just a plain, simple mess.

They had 4.5 stars at one point.  They now have 3.9 stars:

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.firefox&hl=en_CA&gl=US

Do you know how hard you have to work, to drag something down from 4.5, to 3.9, in a month, with almost 4M users?

I honestly don't think they could do worse, if it was intentional sabotage by some hostile insider.

And it's endless garbage like this from Firefox.

What firefox sees:

"OMG!  Chrome is gaining ground!  Quick, turf everything that is unique on our platform, that is different from Chrome.  We must be just like them"

What outsiders see:

"Great, everything I cared about, unique to firefox is now gone.  Plus it's slower, buggier, and they keep changing everything around on every single release.  Great.  Time to move on."

You don't compete with the giant, by being the giant.  You etch out a unique market.

Meanwhile, Firefox did the precise opposite, and removed their uniqueness.

They aren't long for this world.

quotes.text:
>> iPhone users cannot set another browser as the default browser

> iOS 14: Here’s an early look at how you’ll be able to change default apps

I'm not sure you're talking about the same thing.  IIRC, Apple forbids other browser engines, but allows alternative browser apps that use the Safari engine.

For instance: Firefox for iOS exists (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/firefox-private-safe-browser/id989804926), but it's basically just an integration of Safari with Firefox services:

>  It is the first Firefox-branded browser not to use the Gecko layout engine as is used in Firefox for desktop and mobile. Apple's policies require all iOS apps that browse the web to use the built-in WebKit rendering framework and WebKit JavaScript, so using Gecko is not possible. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firefox_for_iOS)
